2. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that the star witness has been examined in the trial and has not support the story as set out in the charge-sheet, thus, there remains no incriminating material on the basis of which further incarceration of the petitioner can be allowed.
No case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

3. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
4. I have considered the submissions made by both the parties and have perused the material available on record.
5. The star witness as well as her parents have been examined in the trial as PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 respectively and they have not supported the story set out by the prosecution rather turned hostile.
Thus, there seems no justification to allow further incarceration of the petitioner as well as looking to the fact that there is high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude.
In light of these facts and circumstances, it is deemed suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner in the present matter.

6. Accordingly, the instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner [2024:RJ-JD:41643] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-12553/2024] as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
(FARJAND ALI),J 39-Ravi Khandelwal Powered by TCPDF (www.tcpdf.org)
